developers.name: Yonatan Sompolinsky
developers.activity: Founder of Kaspa. Postdoctoral researcher in computer science at Harvard University. Lead author of the foundational PHANTOM GHOSTDAG paper that introduced a scalable generalization of Nakamoto consensus. Driving protocol research, BlockDAG topology specifications, and the academic roadmap. Coordinates with the international rust-kaspa rewrite team via the public Kaspa research forum and weekly community AMAs.

developers.name: Aviv Zohar
developers.activity: Co-founder of Kaspa and co-author of the GHOSTDAG paper. Associate professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem with two decades of published research on Bitcoin's selfish-mining vulnerability and DAG-based consensus. Leading the consensus protocol's formal verification effort and supervising graduate students who contribute to the kaspad codebase.

developers.name: Michael Sutton
developers.activity: Lead protocol developer. Architecting the kaspad reference implementation in Go, with 20+ commits per week across consensus, mempool, and networking layers. Coordinating the ongoing rust-kaspa migration aimed at unlocking 10+ blocks per second and the path toward 32 BPS targeted by the DAGKnight upgrade.

narrativeAtSnapshot: Kaspa is a proof-of-work Layer 1 cryptocurrency built on the GHOSTDAG consensus protocol — a BlockDAG architecture that generalizes Nakamoto consensus to allow multiple parallel blocks to coexist and be ordered, rather than orphaned. The mainnet launched on November 7, 2021 with no premine, no ICO, no developer allocation, and no venture funding — a pure fair launch where the founders mined alongside the community from block zero. At snapshot, the network has been live for approximately 13 months, currently producing one block per second with an ambitious roadmap to reach 10 BPS through the ongoing rust-kaspa rewrite and ultimately 32 BPS via the proposed DAGKnight upgrade. The founding team is unusually academic for a PoW project: Dr. Yonatan Sompolinsky (Harvard postdoc) and Prof. Aviv Zohar (Hebrew University) co-authored the foundational PHANTOM GHOSTDAG paper that the protocol implements, building on Sompolinsky's earlier Inclusive Blockchain Protocols work that has been cited in Bitcoin core development discussions. Michael Sutton leads protocol engineering, driving the kaspad Go implementation and the rust-kaspa migration aimed at unlocking the throughput targets. KAS has no smart contract layer — it is a pure monetary asset with a fixed emission curve that approximately halves yearly, designed to mimic Bitcoin's monetary policy while delivering radically faster confirmation times. The community is organic and largely composed of CPU/GPU miners who joined during the fair-launch era; there is no marketing budget and no centralized treasury to deploy. The bear case is substantive. KAS launches into the deepest bear market since 2018: the FTX collapse three weeks before the snapshot has cratered crypto liquidity, retail attention is at multi-year lows, and PoW assets in particular face an ideological backlash post-Merge as Ethereum's transition to PoS has reframed PoW as environmentally indefensible. With no smart contract layer, Kaspa has no DeFi, no NFTs, no stablecoin integration, and no on-chain revenue mechanism — its value proposition rests entirely on the bet that a faster Bitcoin-style monetary asset can carve out market share against an entrenched incumbent worth 1000x its market cap. The fair launch that protects the protocol from regulatory and centralization concerns also means there is no foundation, no marketing team, and no business development function to drive exchange listings or institutional adoption. The rust-kaspa rewrite is incomplete; the DAGKnight upgrade is research-stage; and the entire economic security model depends on attracting and retaining a sufficient PoW miner base while emissions decline yearly. Competitors in the fast-finality PoW niche (Alephium, Nervos) have made similar pitches without traction, and the dominant narrative in crypto winter 2022 is restaking and L2s, not novel L1 monetary assets.
